name: classic french lentils
instructions:
The classic french le puy lentil side — REDEEMED (was briefly retired; see notes). The whole point: a SIDE you can throw into an instapot WITHOUT a multi-stage stew flavor-building process. No sauté, minimal liquid, and the secret finish is SHERRY VINEGAR + BUTTER.

SERVES 4 as a side.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 1 cup dried LE PUY LENTILS, rinsed (the small dark-green french lentils — they hold their shape; don't sub red or brown)
- 1 small yellow onion, chopped — NOT sautéed
- 1 carrot, chopped — NOT sautéed
- 1 celery stalk, chopped — NOT sautéed
- 2-3 garlic cloves, chopped — NOT sautéed
- 1 BAY LEAF (important)
- chicken stock + water — JUST ENOUGH TO COVER the lentils (see the liquid rule)
- salt (go light if the stock is salted) and black pepper

FINISH:
- SHERRY VINEGAR (must be sherry — see notes)
- BUTTER (necessary)
- DRIED TARRAGON (the best herbal finish here)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. EVERYTHING IN THE POT RAW: lentils, chopped onion/garlic/celery/carrot, bay leaf. No sauté step — especially in an instapot, just chopped up and thrown in is fine.
2. LIQUID: chicken stock + water to JUST COVER the lentils — no more. It cooks down to a lentil SIDE, not a stew.
3. PRESSURE COOK: high, 13 minutes (current practice; maybe 15 — see the timing note).
4. FINISH: fish out the bay leaf. SHERRY VINEGAR + BUTTER stirred through hot, dried tarragon, salt and pepper to taste.
notes:
=== REDEEMED (SEPTEMBER 2026) ===

Retired after the first cook (soffrito + broth boring; cream/mustard/vinegar too much; submerged format read as a failed stew; 'no slot left to win') — then redeemed with the discoveries below. The retirement diagnosis was right ('this doesn't want to be a stew') and every fix follows from it: minimal liquid, no flavor-building stages, and a finish that seasons a SIDE rather than building a stew.

=== THE SECRET — SHERRY VINEGAR + BUTTER ===

The secret ingredient pair is SHERRY VINEGAR AND BUTTER — not red wine vinegar, and not mustard (the first cook's dijon + red-wine finish is overturned). It MUST be sherry — other vinegars are TOO HARSH. And the butter is NECESSARY. (Against the old canonical-finish question: the peasant-classical butter-plus-vinegar answer beat the bistro dijon-vinaigrette answer — with the vinegar upgraded to sherry.)

=== THE LIQUID RULE — JUST COVER, NO MORE ===

Fill the pot with just enough chicken stock + water to COVER the lentils, so it cooks down to a LENTIL SIDE and not a stew. The first cook's too-easy-to-become-soup problem was a liquid-quantity problem.

=== NO SAUTÉ — EVERYTHING RAW IN THE POT ===

The onion/garlic/celery/carrot do NOT get sautéed beforehand. Especially in an instapot: chopped up and thrown in with a bay leaf is fine. This is the point of the recipe — no multi-stage flavor building.

=== HERBS — DRIED TARRAGON IS THE FINISH; BAY LEAF IN THE COOK ===

DRIED TARRAGON is the best herbal finish here — better than thyme, certainly better than rosemary or parsley. I like tarragon in this dish MORE than I like it in chicken stews. BAY LEAF is important in the cook itself.

=== PRESSURE TIMING — 13 MIN, MAYBE 15; PRESOAK OPEN QUESTION ===

Current practice: 13 MINUTES at high pressure. Might bump to 15 — the risk at longer times is DESTROYING THE CARROTS, not the lentils (le puy holds; the vegetables are the fragile part). OPEN QUESTION: perhaps a PRESOAK + 10 minutes at high pressure is better — soaked lentils cook faster, which would spare the carrots. Untested.

=== FIRST COOK — HISTORICAL RESULTS (KEPT FOR THE RECORD) ===

- PRESSURE TIME: 8 min high wasn't enough; +3 was sort of enough (superseded by the 13-min current practice above).
- The dijon + red wine vinegar finish read great on a spoonful but didn't hold up — superseded by sherry + butter.
- Rosemary would be awful here — still clashing.

=== LE PUY SPECIFICALLY ===

Le puy lentils hold their shape through cooking — the identity of the dish. Standard brown lentils go soft and muddy; red lentils dissolve entirely (wrong dish).

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[french-lentil-salad]]: the cold expression of french lentils (cream vinaigrette + endives). This is the warm side.
- [[mushroomed-lentils-french]]: the rich gravy-core cousin — that's the stew; this is deliberately not one.
- [[jaffrey-mint-lentils]]: the indian whole-lentil counterpart.
- [[caraway-tomato-stew]]: the other place sherry vinegar is queued (the iberian swing).
why_i_like_this_recipe: It's a side that can be thrown into an instapot without a multi-stage stew flavor-building process.
